Button.name: Button
Button.description:
A button built on Base UI's unstyled `Button` primitive.

Styling is driven entirely by `data-*` attributes and `--pui-button-*`
custom properties, so it can be re-skinned from plain CSS or targeted with
Tailwind arbitrary variants (`data-[variant=solid]:...`) without wrapping.

props.name: className
props.description:
Additional class name(s). Applied after the internal styles so consumer
utilities (e.g. Tailwind) win without needing `!important`.

props.name: focusableWhenDisabled
props.description:
Keep the button focusable while it is disabled. A native `disabled`
button is blurred by the browser, which drops focus to `<body>` and loses
the user's place in the tab order — and takes `aria-busy` and
`loadingLabel` out of earshot with it. Left unset, this turns itself on
for the duration of `loading` so the busy state is actually announced;
pass it explicitly to override.

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Stretch the button to fill the width of its container.

props.name: iconOnly
props.description:
Render as a square button sized for a single icon. Enforces the 24px
minimum hit target from WCAG SC 2.5.8. Always pair with `aria-label`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Show a busy indicator and block interaction. The label keeps its space so
the button cannot resize mid-interaction.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description:
Announced to assistive technology while `loading` is true. Without it, a
screen reader user gets no signal that anything is happening.

props.name: size
props.description:
Size of the button. Actual dimensions also follow the ambient
`data-pui-density` setting.

props.name: tone
props.description:
Which semantic colour set the button draws from. Combines freely with
`variant` — `tone="danger" variant="outline"` is a low-emphasis
destructive action.

props.name: variant
props.description: How much visual weight the button carries.

Checkbox.name: Checkbox
Checkbox.description:
A checkbox built on Base UI's unstyled `Checkbox` primitive.

The root renders a `<span>` plus a hidden `<input>` beside it, so it carries
no accessible name of its own — wrap it in a `<label>`, pair it with a
`<label htmlFor>` (see `nativeButton`), or put it inside a `Field.Root`.

State is exposed on `data-*` attributes (`data-checked`, `data-unchecked`,
`data-indeterminate`, `data-disabled`, `data-readonly`, and the `Field`
validity attributes) on both the root and the indicator, and every visual
decision is a `--pui-checkbox-*` custom property, so it can be re-skinned
from plain CSS or targeted with Tailwind arbitrary variants
(`data-[indeterminate]:...`) without wrapping.

props.name: checked
props.description:
Whether the checkbox is currently ticked. Pairs with `onCheckedChange` for
a controlled checkbox; use `defaultChecked` for an uncontrolled one.

props.name: className
props.description:
Additional class name(s). Applied after the internal styles so consumer
utilities (e.g. Tailwind) win without needing `!important`.

props.name: defaultChecked
props.description: Whether the checkbox starts ticked when uncontrolled.

props.name: indeterminate
props.description:
Mixed state: neither ticked nor unticked. Renders a dash instead of a
tick and sets `data-indeterminate` on both the root and the indicator.
Independent of `checked` — a checkbox that is indeterminate submits
whatever `checked` says it submits.

props.name: indicatorClassName
props.description:
Additional class name(s) for the indicator — the element that holds the
tick. Applied after the internal styles.

props.name: nativeButton
props.description:
Set to `true` when `render` replaces the root with a real `<button>`.
The root is a `<span>` by default so that an enclosing `<label>` stays
valid HTML; for the sibling-label pattern (`<label htmlFor>` + `id`) pass
`nativeButton render={<button />}` instead. With `nativeButton`, `id`
lands on the root element rather than on the hidden input.

props.name: parent
props.description:
Marks this checkbox as the one that controls every other checkbox in the
group. Only works inside a `CheckboxGroup` that has been given `value`
and `allValues`; outside one it does nothing at all. The group drives the
indeterminate state when only some children are ticked.

props.name: size
props.description:
Size of the box. The tick scales with it, so the mark keeps its optical
weight at every size.

props.name: tone
props.description:
Which semantic colour set the checked fill draws from. Inside a
`Field.Root` an invalid field overrides this with the danger palette, so
a validation error always reads as an error.

CheckboxGroup.name: CheckboxGroup
CheckboxGroup.description:
Shared state for a series of `Checkbox`es, built on Base UI's
`CheckboxGroup` primitive.

The group has no implicit accessible name — give it `aria-labelledby`
pointing at a heading, or render it as a `Fieldset.Root` with a
`Fieldset.Legend`.

props.name: allValues
props.description:
Values of *all* checkboxes in the group, ticked or not. Needed only for a
parent checkbox: it is how the group knows the difference between "some"
and "all" and therefore when the parent is indeterminate.

props.name: className
props.description:
Additional class name(s). Applied after the internal styles so consumer
utilities (e.g. Tailwind) win without needing `!important`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Values of the checkboxes that start ticked when uncontrolled.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every checkbox in the group.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Direction the checkboxes are laid out in. Horizontal groups wrap.

props.name: value
props.description:
Values of the checkboxes that are ticked. Pairs with `onValueChange` for
a controlled group; use `defaultValue` for an uncontrolled one. Required
if any child uses the `parent` prop.

DialogTrigger.name: DialogTrigger
DialogTrigger.description:
A button that opens the dialog.

Renders a `<button>`. Pass `render={<Button />}` to compose it with a
styled button — the trigger's own neutral styling steps aside when `render`
is present, so the two never fight over the cascade.

props.name: className
props.description:
Additional class name(s). Applied after the internal styles so consumer
utilities (e.g. Tailwind) win without needing `!important`.

AlertDialogTrigger.name: AlertDialogTrigger
AlertDialogTrigger.description:
A button that opens the alert dialog.

Renders a `<button>`. Identical to `Dialog.Trigger` except that it accepts
an `AlertDialog` handle.

props.name: className
props.description:
Additional class name(s). Applied after the internal styles so consumer
utilities (e.g. Tailwind) win without needing `!important`.

DialogPopup.name: DialogPopup
DialogPopup.description:
The dialog surface, together with the three wrappers it always needs:
`Portal` → `Backdrop` + `Viewport` → `Popup`. Collapsing them into one
component keeps the common case to a single element while leaving every
Base UI `Popup` prop (`initialFocus`, `finalFocus`, `render`, …) available.

`Title`, `Description` and `Close` must be rendered *inside* this component:
that is what auto-wires `aria-labelledby` / `aria-describedby`, and a close
button outside the popup is unreachable to touch screen-reader users.

The same component serves `AlertDialog` — Base UI's alert dialog re-exports
these exact parts.

props.name: backdrop
props.description:
Render the scrim behind the popup. Turn it off for a non-modal dialog
that should leave the page visibly usable.

props.name: backdropClassName
props.description:
Additional class name(s) for the backdrop element. The popup's own
`className` cannot reach it, since the backdrop is a sibling rendered
inside this component.

props.name: className
props.description:
Additional class name(s) for the popup itself. Applied after the internal
styles so consumer utilities (e.g. Tailwind) win without needing
`!important`.

props.name: container
props.type: HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | RefObject<HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | null> | null
props.description:
Element the portal renders into. Defaults to `document.body`; set it when
the dialog must live inside a specific stacking or shadow root.

props.name: forceBackdrop
props.description:
Render the backdrop even when this dialog is nested inside another one.
Base UI suppresses nested backdrops by default — the parent dims itself
through `[data-nested-dialog-open]` instead — so only set this when a
nested dialog genuinely needs its own scrim.

props.name: keepMounted
props.description:
Keep the portal — and therefore the popup — in the DOM while the dialog
is closed. Needed when something inside must stay mounted (an iframe, a
media element, uncommitted form state).

props.name: size
props.description:
Maximum width of the popup. `"fullscreen"` drops the radius and the
viewport padding and lets the surface fill the screen, which is the
usual mobile treatment for a long form.

props.name: viewportClassName
props.description:
Additional class name(s) for the scrollable viewport that positions the
popup. Use it to change alignment (e.g. pin the dialog to the top), or to
re-point `--pui-dialog-z-index` — it defaults to 40, one band under the
anchored popups, so a `Select` or `Tooltip` inside a dialog stays above
it. The backdrop reads `--pui-dialog-backdrop-z-index` (39) from
`backdropClassName`, since it is the viewport's sibling.

DialogTitle.name: DialogTitle
DialogTitle.description:
The dialog's accessible name.

Renders an `<h2>`. Inside `Dialog.Popup` it is wired up as the popup's
`aria-labelledby` automatically; every dialog should have one.

props.name: className
props.description:
Additional class name(s). Applied after the internal styles so consumer
utilities (e.g. Tailwind) win without needing `!important`.

DialogDescription.name: DialogDescription
DialogDescription.description:
A short explanation of what the dialog is for. Renders a `

`. Inside `Dialog.Popup` it becomes the popup's `aria-describedby`, so it is announced after the title.

props.name: className
props.description:
Additional class name(s). Applied after the internal styles so consumer
utilities (e.g. Tailwind) win without needing `!important`.

DialogClose.name: DialogClose
DialogClose.description:
A button that closes the dialog.

Renders a `<button>`. Keep it inside `Dialog.Popup`: in a modal dialog the
rest of the page is inert, and a touch screen-reader user has no other way
out. Pass `render={<Button />}` to compose it with a styled button — the
close button's own neutral styling steps aside when `render` is present.

props.name: className
props.description:
Additional class name(s). Applied after the internal styles so consumer
utilities (e.g. Tailwind) win without needing `!important`.

props.name: iconOnly
props.description:
Render as a square button sized for a single icon — the corner "×"
treatment. Enforces the 24px minimum hit target from WCAG SC 2.5.8.
Always pair with `aria-label`, since there is no text to announce.

DialogFooter.name: DialogFooter
DialogFooter.description:
The action row at the bottom of a dialog.

A plain `<div>` — not a Base UI part — that supplies the standard spacing
and alignment for the confirm/cancel buttons. In a `size="fullscreen"`
dialog it sinks to the bottom edge.

props.name: align
props.description:
How the actions are distributed along the footer. `"between"` is the
pattern for a destructive action pushed away from the safe one.

props.name: className
props.description:
Additional class name(s). Applied after the internal styles so consumer
utilities (e.g. Tailwind) win without needing `!important`.

SelectLabel.name: SelectLabel
SelectLabel.description:
A visible label wired to the trigger. This is the preferred way to give a
select its accessible name — Base UI renders a `<div>` and associates it
with `aria-labelledby`, so clicking it focuses the trigger without opening
the popup. When no visible label is rendered, put `aria-label` on
`<Select.Trigger>` instead.

props.name: className
props.description:
Additional class name(s). Applied after the internal styles so consumer
utilities (e.g. Tailwind) win without needing `!important`.

SelectTrigger.name: SelectTrigger
SelectTrigger.description:
The button that opens the popup. Renders a native `<button>`.

Give it `<Select.Value>` and `<Select.Icon>` as children. It must have an
accessible name: either render a `<Select.Label>` inside the same
`<Select.Root>`, or pass `aria-label` here. In development the trigger
warns once if it ends up with neither.

props.name: className
props.description:
Additional class name(s). Applied after the internal styles so consumer
utilities (e.g. Tailwind) win without needing `!important`.

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Stretch the trigger to fill the width of its container.

props.name: size
props.description:
Size of the trigger. Actual dimensions also follow the ambient
`data-pui-density` setting.

props.name: variant
props.description:
How much visual weight the trigger carries. `outline` reads as a form
control, `soft` as a filled field, `ghost` as an inline affordance.

SelectValue.name: SelectValue
SelectValue.description:
The selected item's label inside the trigger. Renders a `<span>`.

By default this renders the raw `value`. Pass `items` to `<Select.Root>` to
render the matching label instead, or pass a function as `children` to
format it yourself.

A `placeholder` cannot be cleared by the user once a value is chosen. If the
selection has to be clearable from the popup, render an item whose value is
`null` instead of using `placeholder`.

props.name: className
props.description:
Additional class name(s). Applied after the internal styles so consumer
utilities (e.g. Tailwind) win without needing `!important`.

SelectIcon.name: SelectIcon
SelectIcon.description:
The affordance that marks the trigger as a select. Renders a `<span>`, and
carries `data-popup-open` so it can react to the popup's state.

Purely decorative — the trigger's own role and `aria-expanded` are what
reach assistive technology.

props.name: children
props.description:
Icon to render. Defaults to a caret pair, which stays correct whichever
side the popup ends up on — including `alignItemWithTrigger` mode, where
it opens over the trigger and has no side at all.

props.name: className
props.description:
Additional class name(s). Applied after the internal styles so consumer
utilities (e.g. Tailwind) win without needing `!important`.

SelectPopup.name: SelectPopup
SelectPopup.description:
The floating surface holding the list of items.

This one part renders the whole floating half of Base UI's anatomy —
`Portal` → (`Backdrop`) → `Positioner` → `Popup` → `ScrollUpArrow` +
`List` + `ScrollDownArrow` — because those elements are meaningless apart
and each one has a job the styles depend on: the positioner owns
`--anchor-width` and `--available-height`, the popup owns the surface, and
the list owns scrolling (which is what the scroll arrows measure).

props.name: align
props.description:
How the popup aligns along the chosen side. Ignored while
`alignItemWithTrigger` is in effect.

props.name: alignItemWithTrigger
props.description:
Whether the popup overlaps the trigger so the selected item's text lines
up with the trigger's value text. While this is active `data-side` is
`"none"` on both the positioner and the popup, `side`/`align`/`sideOffset`
are ignored, and the enter/exit transition is suppressed. Base UI also
disables it automatically for touch input and when the viewport is too
tight, in which case ordinary side placement takes over.

props.name: alignOffset
props.description:
Extra offset in pixels along the alignment axis. Ignored while
`alignItemWithTrigger` is in effect.

props.name: backdrop
props.description:
Render a dimming layer behind the popup. Off by default — a select is a
menu, not a dialog — but useful on small screens where the popup covers
most of the page.

props.name: children
props.description:
The items, separators and groups to render. They are placed inside
`<Select.List>`, which is the element that actually scrolls.

props.name: className
props.description:
Additional class name(s) for the popup surface. Applied after the
internal styles so consumer utilities win without needing `!important`.

props.name: collisionPadding
props.description: Space to keep between the popup and the edge of its collision boundary.

props.name: container
props.type: HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | RefObject<HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | null> | null
props.description: Render the popup into a different container instead of `<body>`.

props.name: finalFocus
props.type: boolean | RefObject<HTMLElement | null> | ((closeType: InteractionType) => boolean | void | HTMLElement | null)
props.description:
Where focus goes when the popup closes. There is no `initialFocus`
counterpart on a select popup — Base UI always moves focus to the
highlighted item on open.

props.name: positionerClassName
props.description:
Additional class name(s) for the positioner — the absolutely positioned
wrapper around the popup. Use this for `z-index` or a `min-height` that
tunes how often `alignItemWithTrigger` falls back.

props.name: scrollArrows
props.description:
Render the hover-to-scroll arrows at the top and bottom of the list. They
are a pointer convenience only: Base UI does not render them for touch
input, and the list scrolls by wheel, drag, keyboard and typeahead
regardless, so no item is ever reachable only through them.

props.name: side
props.description:
Which side of the trigger the popup opens on. Ignored while
`alignItemWithTrigger` is in effect.

props.name: sideOffset
props.description:
Gap in pixels between the trigger and the popup. Ignored while
`alignItemWithTrigger` is in effect.

SelectItem.name: SelectItem
SelectItem.description:
One option in the popup. Renders a `<div>` with `role="option"`.

`data-highlighted` is the focus analogue here: Base UI moves real DOM focus
between items with a roving tabindex, and (with `highlightItemOnHover`,
which is on by default) pointer hover sets the same attribute. Because the
list is a clipping scroll container, the focus ring is applied inset via
`data-focus-inset` so `overflow` cannot crop it.

props.name: children
props.description:
The item's label. Rendered inside `<Select.ItemText>`, which is what
`<Select.Value>` mirrors in the trigger and what typeahead matches on.

props.name: className
props.description:
Additional class name(s). Applied after the internal styles so consumer
utilities (e.g. Tailwind) win without needing `!important`.

props.name: disabled
props.description:
Whether the item ignores user interaction. Disabled items stay in the
list and stay announced; typeahead skips them.

props.name: indicator
props.description:
What marks the item as selected. Rendered inside
`<Select.ItemIndicator>`, which only mounts while the item is selected.

props.name: label
props.description: Plain-text label used for typeahead when `children` is not a string.

props.name: value
props.description:
The value this item selects. `null` is a legitimate value and is how you
offer a "clear the selection" row inside the list.

SelectGroup.name: SelectGroup
SelectGroup.description:
Groups related items under a heading. Renders a `<div>` with
`role="group"`; Base UI associates it with the `<Select.GroupLabel>` inside
it automatically, so the heading is announced with its members.

props.name: className
props.description:
Additional class name(s). Applied after the internal styles so consumer
utilities (e.g. Tailwind) win without needing `!important`.

SelectGroupLabel.name: SelectGroupLabel
SelectGroupLabel.description:
The heading for a `<Select.Group>`. Renders a `<div>`, indented past the
indicator column so its text lines up with the item text rather than with
the check marks.

props.name: className
props.description:
Additional class name(s). Applied after the internal styles so consumer
utilities (e.g. Tailwind) win without needing `!important`.

SelectSeparator.name: SelectSeparator
SelectSeparator.description:
A divider between groups of items. Renders a `<div>` with
`role="separator"`, so it is exposed to assistive technology rather than
being a purely visual line.

props.name: className
props.description:
Additional class name(s). Applied after the internal styles so consumer
utilities (e.g. Tailwind) win without needing `!important`.

props.name: orientation
props.description:
Orientation of the rule. A select list is vertical, so the separator
between two groups runs horizontally.

Switch.name: Switch

props.name: className
props.description:
Additional class name(s) for the track. Applied after the internal styles
so consumer utilities (e.g. Tailwind) win without needing `!important`.

props.name: id
props.description:
The id of the hidden `<input>` element — or of the root element when
`nativeButton` is `true`. Point a sibling `<label htmlFor>` at whichever
of the two your `nativeButton` setting produces.

props.name: nativeButton
props.description:
Whether the rendered element is a native `<button>`. Base UI defaults
this to `false` here — the opposite of trigger-style parts — because the
root renders a `<span>` so that an enclosing `<label>` stays valid HTML.

Set it (together with `render={<button />}`) for the sibling-label
`htmlFor`/`id` pattern. Note that it also moves `id`: with `nativeButton`
the `id` lands on the root element, otherwise on the hidden input.

props.name: size
props.description:
Size of the switch. Track, thumb and travel distance all scale together,
so the thumb always lands flush against the end of the track.

props.name: stateIcon
props.description:
Draw a checkmark inside the thumb while the switch is on.

This is the switch's non-positional state cue, and it is why the default
is `true`: a user who cannot perceive the thumb sliding still gets a
glyph appearing. Turning it off leaves colour as the only cue that does
not depend on noticing movement.

props.name: thumbClassName
props.description: Additional class name(s) for the thumb, for the same reason.

TabsRoot.name: TabsRoot
TabsRoot.description:
Groups the tab strip and its panels.

Note the Base UI default: `defaultValue` is `0`, an *index*, not the first
tab's string value. With string values and no `defaultValue`, Base UI emits
an automatic `onValueChange` with reason `'initial'` to correct itself, so
always pass `defaultValue` (or `value`) pointing at an **enabled** tab —
during server rendering a disabled first tab is not skipped. `null` is a
legal "nothing active" value and is deliberately not normalised away.

props.name: className
props.description:
Additional class name(s). Applied after the internal styles so consumer
utilities (e.g. Tailwind) win without needing `!important`.

props.name: variant
props.description:
Which indicator treatment the tab strip uses. `"line"` draws a rail with a
sliding underline; `"pill"` draws a filled pill that slides behind the
active tab. Both are the same indicator element moved by the same CSS
variables — only the geometry differs.

TabsList.name: TabsList
TabsList.description:
The tab strip. Must contain the `Indicator`, which is positioned against
this element — the stylesheet gives it `position: relative` for exactly that
reason.

props.name: activateOnFocus
props.description:
Whether arrow-key focus also activates the tab it lands on. Left `false`
so arrow keys only move focus and activation happens on Enter or Space —
automatic activation loads every panel the user arrows past, which is
hostile when a panel fetches data.

props.name: className
props.description:
Additional class name(s). Applied after the internal styles so consumer
utilities (e.g. Tailwind) win without needing `!important`.

props.name: loopFocus
props.description: Whether arrow-key focus wraps from the last tab back to the first.

TabsTab.name: TabsTab

props.name: className
props.description:
Additional class name(s). Applied after the internal styles so consumer
utilities (e.g. Tailwind) win without needing `!important`.

TabsIndicator.name: TabsIndicator
TabsIndicator.description:
The sliding marker. Base UI publishes the active tab's geometry on this
element as `--active-tab-left` / `--active-tab-top` / `--active-tab-width` /
`--active-tab-height` (already px values, consumed directly, never wrapped
in `calc()` as raw numbers) and the stylesheet turns those into a `translate`
+ size transition.

Renders inside `Tabs.List`, never outside it.

props.name: className
props.description:
Additional class name(s). Applied after the internal styles so consumer
utilities (e.g. Tailwind) win without needing `!important`.

props.name: renderBeforeHydration
props.description:
Whether to emit a tiny inline script that positions the indicator before
React hydrates. Defaults to `true` here rather than Base UI's `false`:
without it a server-rendered tab strip shows no indicator at all until
hydration finishes, which reads as a broken selection.

TabsPanel.name: TabsPanel
TabsPanel.description:
The content region for one tab. Base UI gives it `tabIndex={0}` so keyboard
users can reach the content directly after the strip — which is why it
carries the focus ring as well as the Tab does.

props.name: className
props.description:
Additional class name(s). Applied after the internal styles so consumer
utilities (e.g. Tailwind) win without needing `!important`.

props.name: keepMounted
props.description:
Whether the panel stays in the DOM while hidden. Required if you want the
exit transition to play, or if the panel holds scroll position or
uncommitted form state that should survive a round trip.

TooltipProvider.name: TooltipProvider
TooltipProvider.description:
Shares one hover delay across every tooltip beneath it. Renders no DOM
element.

Mount it once near the root of the app. Without it each tooltip waits out
its own delay, so sweeping across a toolbar feels sticky.

props.name: children
props.description: The subtree that shares this delay.

props.name: closeDelay
props.description: How long to wait before closing a tooltip, in milliseconds.

props.name: delay
props.description:
How long to wait before opening a tooltip, in milliseconds. Applies to
every tooltip below this provider; an individual `Tooltip.Trigger` can
still override it.

props.name: timeout
props.description:
Grouping window, in milliseconds. If one tooltip closes and another opens
within this window, the second one appears instantly instead of waiting
out `delay` again — which is what makes a row of icon buttons feel like a
single toolbar rather than a series of separate waits.

TooltipRoot.name: TooltipRoot
TooltipRoot.description:
Groups one tooltip's trigger and popup. Renders no DOM element, so it takes
no `className`, `style` or `ref`.

props.name: actionsRef
props.description:
Imperative escape hatch. `unmount()` forces the popup out of the DOM (use
it when an exit animation is driven externally); `close()` closes the
tooltip.

props.name: children
props.description:
The trigger and popup for this tooltip. May also be a render function
receiving `{ payload }` from the trigger that opened the tooltip.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description:
Whether the tooltip is open when it first mounts. For a controlled
tooltip use `open` instead.

props.name: defaultTriggerId
props.description:
The initially attached trigger id. Pairs with `defaultOpen` the way
`triggerId` pairs with `open`.

props.name: disabled
props.description:
Whether this tooltip is disabled. Disables the tooltip only — the trigger
element stays fully interactive and does not receive the `disabled`
attribute.

props.name: disableHoverablePopup
props.description:
Whether the popup can be hovered without closing. Off by default: a
tooltip is not meant to hold interactive content, and a hoverable popup
gets in the way of the content beneath it.

props.name: handle
props.description:
Associates this tooltip with detached triggers created through
`Tooltip.createHandle()`, so one popup can serve several triggers that
live elsewhere in the tree.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description:
Called when the tooltip wants to open or close. The second argument
carries the reason (`'trigger-hover'`, `'trigger-focus'`,
`'trigger-press'`, `'outside-press'`, `'escape-key'`, `'disabled'`,
`'imperative-action'`, `'none'`) and can `cancel()` the change.

props.name: onOpenChangeComplete
props.description:
Called after the open or close transition has finished. Use this rather
than a timer when work has to wait for the popup to actually leave.

props.name: open
props.description:
Whether the tooltip is currently open. Pass this together with
`onOpenChange` to control the tooltip.

props.name: trackCursorAxis
props.description:
Which axis the tooltip follows the cursor on. `'both'` turns it into a
cursor-tracking label; combine with `side="bottom"` for the usual feel.

props.name: triggerId
props.description:
The trigger the tooltip is attached to, for controlled multi-trigger
setups. There is no separate `onTriggerIdChange` — derive the new id from
`eventDetails.trigger` inside `onOpenChange`.

TooltipTrigger.name: TooltipTrigger
TooltipTrigger.description:
The element the tooltip is attached to. Renders a `<button>`.

**This trigger must carry its own accessible name.** The tooltip is a
visual affordance only — see the note on {@link Tooltip} — so an icon-only
trigger needs an `aria-label` that closely matches the tooltip's text.
Screen reader users get the `aria-label` and nothing else.

Unlike `Popover.Trigger` and `Menu.Trigger`, this part has **no
`nativeButton` prop**; it always renders button semantics. Compose it with
an existing control through `render` instead.

props.name: className
props.description:
Additional class name(s). Applied after the internal styles so consumer
utilities (e.g. Tailwind) win without needing `!important`.

props.name: closeDelay
props.description: How long to wait before closing, in milliseconds.

props.name: closeOnClick
props.description:
Whether clicking the trigger closes the tooltip. Leave it on for triggers
that do something on click — the tooltip has served its purpose by then
and would otherwise sit over the result.

props.name: delay
props.description:
How long to wait before opening, in milliseconds. Overrides the
provider's `delay` for this trigger only.

props.name: disabled
props.description:
Stops this trigger from opening the tooltip. It does **not** apply the
`disabled` attribute to the element, so the button stays focusable and
clickable; style the difference from `data-trigger-disabled`. To disable
the control itself, pass `disabled` through `render`.

props.name: handle
props.description:
Associates a detached trigger with a `Tooltip.Root` that carries the same
handle, created once outside render with `Tooltip.createHandle()`.

props.name: payload
props.description:
Data handed to the tooltip when this trigger opens it, so one popup can
render different content per trigger.

props.name: ref
props.description: Forwarded to the underlying element.

props.name: render
props.description:
Replaces the rendered `<button>` with another element or component —
`render={<Button variant="ghost" />}` is the common case. Note there is
no `nativeButton` prop on this part: it always renders button semantics.

TooltipPopup.name: TooltipPopup
TooltipPopup.description:
The tooltip surface. Renders the portal, the positioner and the popup in
one part, so the common case is a single element in consumer markup.

Keep the content to a short visual label. Anything a user must read to
operate the UI belongs in the page or in a `Popover` — see {@link Tooltip}.

props.name: align
props.description: How the tooltip lines up with the trigger along the chosen side.

props.name: alignOffset
props.description:
Shifts the tooltip along the alignment axis, in pixels, or a function
returning one.

props.name: anchor
props.type: Element | VirtualElement | RefObject<Element | null> | (() => Element | VirtualElement | null) | null
props.description:
The element the tooltip positions against, when it should not be the
trigger.

props.name: arrowPadding
props.description:
Minimum distance, in pixels, the arrow keeps from the tooltip's corners
before it is allowed to sit off-centre (`data-uncentered`).

props.name: className
props.description:
Additional class name(s). Applied after the internal styles so consumer
utilities (e.g. Tailwind) win without needing `!important`.

props.name: collisionAvoidance
props.description:
How the tooltip reacts when it would overflow the boundary — whether it
flips, shifts, or stays put.

props.name: collisionBoundary
props.description: The boundary the tooltip tries to stay inside of.

props.name: collisionPadding
props.description: Space, in pixels, kept between the tooltip and the collision boundary.

props.name: container
props.type: HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | RefObject<HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | null> | null
props.description:
Where the portal renders. Defaults to `document.body`; point it at a
container when the tooltip has to live inside a specific stacking or
shadow root.

props.name: disableAnchorTracking
props.description:
Stops the tooltip re-measuring the anchor on scroll and resize. Cheaper,
but the tooltip drifts if the anchor moves.

props.name: keepMounted
props.description: Keeps the portal in the DOM while the tooltip is closed.

props.name: positionerClassName
props.description:
Additional class name(s) for the positioner element, which owns
placement and `z-index`. Use it to re-stack a single tooltip.

props.name: positionMethod
props.description:
Whether the tooltip is positioned with `position: absolute` or
`position: fixed`.

props.name: side
props.description:
Which side of the trigger to place the tooltip on. Flips automatically to
avoid collisions. `"inline-start"` / `"inline-end"` follow writing
direction.

props.name: sideOffset
props.description:
Gap between trigger and tooltip, in pixels, or a function returning one.
When an `Arrow` is rendered this must exceed the arrow's height or the
arrow will overlap the trigger; the default leaves room for the default
arrow.

props.name: sticky
props.description:
Keeps the tooltip glued to the trigger while it scrolls out of view
instead of letting it detach.

TooltipArrow.name: TooltipArrow
TooltipArrow.description:
The wedge pointing back at the trigger. Render it as the first child of
`Tooltip.Popup`.

It is an SVG rather than the traditional CSS-border triangle on purpose: in
forced-colors mode every border colour is forced to `CanvasText`, and a
border triangle degrades into a filled rectangle. Two flat paths cannot
fail that way.

props.name: children
props.description:
Replaces the built-in wedge. The default SVG inherits the popup's colours
through `--pui-tooltip-bg`, so a custom skin usually needs nothing here.

props.name: className
props.description:
Additional class name(s). Applied after the internal styles so consumer
utilities (e.g. Tailwind) win without needing `!important`.
